## Overview

Extend completed iteration records with scheduled attention-workload and queued-request snapshots for Dynamo performance modeling. Collection is optional, disabled by default and transport-independent. This is the workload layer split from #52061, reusing #61424's scheduling counters rather than implementing them again. Related: #61423, #39979, #38760.

Dependency order: #61690 (timing) → **#61691 (this PR)** → #52061 (FPM exporter), after prerequisite #61424. [Previous layer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61690) · [Next layer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52061) · [Review only this layer](https://github.com/tedzhouhk/vllm/compare/eaa98b274d6e00c897216c835bc273806e8bb48d...03443570fa78e4ae9ca983ee3733b54eb73314a6).

These dependent fork branches preserve their PR numbers/reviews and target `main`, so upstream diffs are cumulative. Review layer-only links and merge/rebase in order; [cross-fork native stacks are unsupported](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-pull-requests).

## Claims

- `--enable-iteration-workload-metrics` derives required timing at startup without enabling verbose logging. There is no separate timing CLI/constructor option and no ZMQ/OTLP dependency. Unsupported required timing fails validation rather than producing untimed records.
- Each completed record joins scheduled counts, prefill/decode attention-context sums and population variances, queued workload and GPU duration for its own iteration. Transport-independent types/accumulation live in `iteration_workload.py`; the reusable Welford helper is in `utils/math_utils.py`. Scheduler metadata is extended rather than rescanning scheduled requests on the default path.
- For prefill with `kv_read=x` and `scheduled_tokens=y`, attention length is `x + y/2`; variance is across those current-iteration lengths, not full prompts. Decode statistics represent logical attention context, not physical KV residency or speculative-token counts.
- Async speculative rejection corrections use existing CPU sampled-token results, preserving the original snapshot, request identity and preemption generation. They add no D2H transfer, events, kernels or sampling changes.
- Queued snapshots preserve FPM v1 conventions: preempted/remote-KV-waiting requests count as queued decode; other waiting requests as queued prefill. Both waiting queues are included without double counting. Normal snapshots follow the associated output; dummy snapshots are captured at submission.
- Timed attention-DP dummy records have empty scheduled work and may contain queued work. EngineCore emits zero-duration idle records at most once per second only after `has_work()` is false, input queues are empty and pending timings have drained. DP work includes coordinated wave state; publisher silence is never used to infer idle. Dummy associations survive beyond the ordinary batch-queue depth.
- The synchronous offline frontend filters idle-only records without dropping control/output messages. Later publication is EngineCore-owned and does not depend on frontend consumption. Self-benchmark orchestration remains in Dynamo.

## Validation

Head `03443570`: 72 focused configuration, collection, scheduler and async-SD tests passed. The final full stack `e0df2bd5` passed 124 focused tests and independent unit/wire checks; counts overlap. Normal hooks and independent replay review passed. This layer's replay only adapts incoming timing fixtures to milliseconds and preserves idle log labels while omitting current KV usage.

A pinned full-stack workload-only GPU case, MRV2 async eager TP1/PP1 with UniProc, proved actual `log_stats=False`, no custom logger, zero iteration log lines and 48 positive records; every raw worker millisecond value matched its generic record. Parent timing and FPM-wire validation are in #61690 and #52061.

The 72-test run included:

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/config/test_observability.py tests/v1/engine/test_iteration_logging.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py tests/v1/metrics/test_iteration_timing.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py::test_iteration_workload_requires_multiprocessing_client \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_iteration_workload_uses_current_chunk_attention_lengths \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_iteration_workload_classifies_all_recompute_chunks_as_prefill \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_disabled_iteration_workload_does_not_allocate_accumulator \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py::test_iteration_workload_matches_async_speculative_execution_context -q
```

This restack includes PR1's readable Future completion, millisecond timing contract and removal of current KV usage from historical per-iteration logs; periodic KV reporting remains. Earlier qualification is retained below at its actual SHAs, not relabeled as current-head evidence. No fresh throughput/multi-GPU claim is made.

## Details

Required timing supports generative CUDA models, `uni`/`mp` executors and out-of-process EngineCore; pooling, non-CUDA, Ray/external-launcher and in-process configurations are rejected. PP measures only the last-stage output worker, not whole-pipeline latency. Best-effort shutdown can discard tails.

Enabled collection adds CPU bookkeeping/queue scans; default-off does not collect these snapshots. Previous native-MTP PP2 qualification covers only MRV2 async eager; other attempted combinations failed on the timing-off baseline. Prior DP oracle checks completed before shutdown, but workers needed force-kill; graceful teardown is not established.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Nonblocking GPU iteration timing shared by both model runners.
+
+Intervals span model execution, sampling and speculative drafting on the
+recorded stream, including host-submission gaps. Independent work on other
+streams and EngineCore scheduling are outside this timing scope.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import queue
+import threading
+from collections import deque
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from copy import copy
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class _PendingTiming:
+    iteration_id: int
+    start_event: Any
+    end_event: Any
+
+
+class IterationTimer:
+    """Pool timing events and collect only completed GPU intervals.
+
+    Output-copy and worker threads may drain concurrently. A contended drain
+    returns immediately instead of delaying the next model execution.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_event_pairs: int,
+        event_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        if num_event_pairs <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("num_event_pairs must be positive")
+        self._event_factory = event_factory or self._make_event
+        self._event_pool: queue.SimpleQueue[tuple[Any, Any]] = queue.SimpleQueue()
+        for _ in range(num_event_pairs):
+            self._event_pool.put((self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()))
+        self._pending: deque[_PendingTiming] = deque()
+        self._active: _PendingTiming | None = None
+        self._pending_lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._drain_lock = threading.Lock()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _make_event() -> torch.Event:
+        return torch.Event(enable_timing=True)
+
+    def start(self, iteration_id: int | None) -> None:
+        if self._active is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("An iteration timing interval is already active")
+        if iteration_id is None:
+            return
+        try:
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_pool.get_nowait()
+        except queue.Empty:
+            # DP dummy steps can outlive the ordinary batch-queue bound.
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "Iteration CUDA event pool exhausted; allocating one extra pair"
+            )
+            start_event, end_event = self._event_factory(), self._event_factory()
+        start_event.record()
+        self._active = _PendingTiming(iteration_id, start_event, end_event)
+
+    def finish(self) -> None:
+        if self._active is None:
+            return
+        pending = self._active
+        self._active = None
+        pending.end_event.record()
+        with self._pending_lock:
+            self._pending.append(pending)
+
+    def cancel(self) -> None:
+        # Discard this pair instead of recycling an event still in flight.
+        self._active = None
+
+    def drain_samples(self) -> tuple[tuple[int, float], ...]:
+        """Return ready (iteration_id, elapsed_ms) pairs without synchronization."""
+        if not self._drain_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+            return ()
+        ready: list[tuple[int, float]] = []
+        try:
+            while True:
+                if not self._pending_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+                    break
+                try:
+                    pending = self._pending[0] if self._pending else None
+                finally:
+                    self._pending_lock.release()
+                if pending is None or not pending.end_event.query():
+                    break
+
+                elapsed_ms = pending.start_event.elapsed_time(pending.end_event)
+                if not self._pending_lock.acquire(blocking=False):
+                    break
+                try:
+                    self._pending.popleft()
+                finally:
+                    self._pending_lock.release()
+                ready.append((pending.iteration_id, elapsed_ms))
+                self._event_pool.put((pending.start_event, pending.end_event))
+        finally:
+            self._drain_lock.release()
+        return tuple(ready)
+
+    def drain_into(self, output: Any) -> Any:
+        """Attach ready samples without mutating shared empty runner outputs.
+
+        Async handles collect their samples later in get_output().
+        """
+        if output is None or not hasattr(output, "iteration_timing_samples"):
+            return output
+        ready = self.drain_samples()
+        if not ready:
+            return output
+        output = copy(output)
+        output.iteration_timing_samples += ready
+        return output
+
+
+def make_iteration_timer(
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    rank: int,
+) -> IterationTimer | None:
+    """Allocate events only when timing is enabled on the model-output rank."""
+    if not vllm_config.observability_config.iteration_timing_enabled:
+        return None
+    parallel_config = vllm_config.parallel_config
+    output_rank = parallel_config.world_size - (
+        parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size
+        * parallel_config.prefill_context_parallel_size
+    )
+    if rank != output_rank:
+        return None
+    return IterationTimer(num_event_pairs=vllm_config.max_concurrent_batches + 1)

+"""Transport-independent workload snapshots for completed engine iterations."""

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field

+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

+from vllm.utils.math_utils import WelfordAccumulator
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.core.sched.interface import SchedulerInterface

+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScheduledIterationWorkload:
+    """Logical context lengths at the start of the scheduled model execution."""
+
+    sum_prefill_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    # Population variance of kv_read + scheduled_tokens / 2, in tokens squared.
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class QueuedIterationWorkload:
+    """Waiting work after output processing, or at dummy/idle submission.
+
+    Preempted requests and requests waiting for remote KV are grouped as
+    queued decode work. This queue category is distinct from the scheduler's
+    execution phase: a resumed request may need prefill recomputation.
+    """
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class IterationWorkloadAccumulator:
+    prefill_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    prefill_lengths: WelfordAccumulator = field(default_factory=WelfordAccumulator)
+    decode_lengths: WelfordAccumulator = field(default_factory=WelfordAccumulator)
+
+    def add_prefill(self, kv_tokens: int, scheduled_tokens: int) -> None:
+        self.prefill_kv_tokens += kv_tokens
+        # Keep half-token attention lengths exact during integer accumulation.
+        self.prefill_lengths.add(2 * kv_tokens + scheduled_tokens)
+
+    def add_decode(self, kv_tokens: int) -> None:
+        self.decode_lengths.add(kv_tokens)
+
+    def snapshot(self) -> ScheduledIterationWorkload:
+        return ScheduledIterationWorkload(
+            sum_prefill_kv_tokens=self.prefill_kv_tokens,
+            var_prefill_length=self.prefill_lengths.variance / 4,
+            sum_decode_kv_tokens=self.decode_lengths.total,
+            var_decode_kv_tokens=self.decode_lengths.variance,
+        )
+
+
+def extract_queued_workload(scheduler: "SchedulerInterface") -> QueuedIterationWorkload:
+    from vllm.v1.request import RequestStatus
+
+    waiting = scheduler.waiting
+    kv_holding_waiting = scheduler.kv_holding_waiting
+    assert waiting is not None
+    assert kv_holding_waiting is not None
+    prefill = WelfordAccumulator()
+    decode = WelfordAccumulator()
+    # Deferred requests are already in these disjoint queues.
+    for request in chain(waiting, kv_holding_waiting):
+        if request.status in (
+            RequestStatus.PREEMPTED,
+            RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS,
+        ):
+            decode.add(request.num_computed_tokens)
+        else:
+            prefill.add(request.num_tokens)
+    return QueuedIterationWorkload(
+        num_prefill_requests=prefill.count,
+        sum_prefill_tokens=prefill.total,
+        var_prefill_length=prefill.variance,
+        num_decode_requests=decode.count,
+        sum_decode_kv_tokens=decode.total,
+        var_decode_kv_tokens=decode.variance,
+    )
